title: Kesko 48-hour challenge brief (scoping draft, not ready to run)

blocks.text: Scoping draft only: no process owner, approved dataset or acceptance criterion has been confirmed.

Scoping draft only. No staff problem, internal owner, approved data or success criterion was supplied, so every direction below is a hypothesis to validate, not a confirmed Kesko need. Do not run a hackathon from this brief until those inputs exist.

Explore whether a small, bounded tool could reduce manual reconciliation work in an area Kesko's team names as a pain point. Candidate areas are drawn from public signals only: integration of acquired Nordic technical-trade operations, and the warehouse and order flows around the Manhattan Associates ActiveWarehouse rollout.

items.text: Dahl technical-trade operations in Sweden, Norway and Denmark, completion targeted by end-2026, with separate brands and units that may need reconciling
Kesko selected ActiveWarehouse for five distribution centres, with a new site in 2029-30

blocks.text: 2. Three directions with proposed acceptance tests
Each test is a proposal to be agreed with a named owner. Baseline numbers must be measured by the client before the event.

rows: A. Order and data reconciliation across units: match order or financial records between two units and flag exceptions
Working prototype reconciles a agreed sample set; exception rate and manual minutes per batch measured against a client-provided baseline
B. Warehouse exception triage: route and summarise stock or order exceptions for a human to action
Prototype classifies a agreed set of historical exceptions; agreement with the client's labelled answers at a threshold the owner sets
C. Acquisition onboarding checklist: a guided workflow that tracks integration tasks across teams
Used by a named pilot group for a defined period; tasks closed on time vs. baseline set by the owner

blocks.text: Numeric thresholds, sample sizes and baselines are placeholders for the client to supply. Any time-saving figure would be an estimate until measured.

items.text: What manual step do people repeat every week when two systems disagree?
Which exception could be surfaced to the right person automatically, with the context already attached?
What would a integration status view look like if it updated itself from existing records?
Where does information get re-keyed between the warehouse system and finance?
Which approval or sign-off could be pre-filled and only checked by a human?
What would the team stop doing if this tool worked in its first week?

blocks.text: One working prototype for one direction, run on approved or synthetic data, with a one-page readout: what it does, the measured result against the agreed test, known limits and the recommended next step. No production deployment, no integration with live systems.

items.text: No access to live customer, supplier or personnel data unless the client approves it in writing beforehand
No changes to production warehouse, ERP or finance systems
No commitments on pricing, timelines or follow-on work
No claims of savings, results or client outcomes beyond what is measured in the event

rows: Confirm owner, data access and acceptance test; brief the team
Build check against acceptance test with client owner
Build core prototype on approved data
Demo to owner; agree next step or stop
Readout delivered; no guaranteed production handover

blocks.text: Staffing: a Velho lead and up to two builders, plus a client owner and a data contact. Names, calendar slots and availability are not yet confirmed and are not assumed here.
Monday delivery is not guaranteed. Event length and scope are subject to agreement.
Cover note (for Velho employee to review and send manually)

blocks.label: Cover note
blocks.text: Hi [name], we noticed Kesko's recent moves in technical trade integration and warehouse tooling. We have a rough 48-hour challenge idea that could test one small reconciliation problem with approved data. Before anything is set, we'd like to understand what your team sees as the most manual step. Would a 30-minute scoping conversation be useful? No commitment, just a shared starting point.
